sections.content: Finding wholesale real estate deals in your local market sounds simple on the surface. But ask any new wholesaler and they'll tell you: knowing where to look makes all the difference. Whether you're just getting started or you've done a few deals and want to scale up, this guide walks you through exactly how to find wholesale real estate deals in your area — consistently and profitably. If you're brand new to the game, check out our [Wholesale Real Estate for Beginners: Complete Guide](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesale-real-estate-beginners-guide) before diving in here.
Why Local Market Knowledge Is Your Biggest Advantage

National wholesalers often compete in dozens of markets at once. That means they're working from data, not relationships. When you focus on your own backyard, you build something they can't buy: local trust. You know which neighborhoods are up-and-coming, which zip codes have high absentee-owner rates, and which property managers are quietly looking for cash deals. This hyper-local edge helps you find deals before anyone else does — and close them faster.
The 6 Best Ways to Find Wholesale Deals in Your Area
1. Direct Mail to Motivated Sellers

Direct mail remains one of the most reliable lead generation strategies in wholesaling. The key is targeting the right lists. Focus on homeowners who are most likely to want a fast, hassle-free sale. The best lists include: absentee owners, pre-foreclosures, probate properties, tax-delinquent homeowners, and owners of vacant properties. A typical direct mail campaign costs between $0.50 and $1.50 per piece. Expect a response rate of 1% to 3% on a cold list. That means if you mail 500 letters, you might get 5 to 15 callbacks — and one or two of those could become deals worth $10,000 or more in assignment fees.

Use hand-addressed yellow letters or postcards with a personal tone. Avoid anything that looks like mass marketing. A simple message like 'I want to buy your house as-is, any condition, fast close' outperforms polished flyers almost every time.
2. Driving for Dollars

This old-school strategy still works. Get in your car and drive through target neighborhoods looking for distressed properties — overgrown lawns, boarded windows, tarps on roofs, piled-up mail, or missing shutters. These visual cues often signal a motivated or absentee owner. Apps like DealMachine let you photograph and log properties on the go, then pull owner contact info immediately. Dedicate just two hours per week to driving for dollars and you can build a list of 50 to 100 potential leads per month in most markets.
3. MLS and Expired Listings

The MLS isn't just for retail buyers. Expired and withdrawn listings represent sellers who tried to sell the traditional way and failed. They're often frustrated, motivated, and open to a faster solution. Partner with a real estate agent who can pull expired listings for you, or get your own license to access the MLS directly. Look for properties that have been sitting for 90-plus days, especially in price ranges below the local median. These sellers are primed for a conversation about a cash offer.
4. Probate and Court Records

Probate properties are inherited homes that heirs often want to sell quickly — especially if they live out of state or can't afford upkeep. Visit your local county courthouse or search your county's online public records to find recently filed probate cases. Send a respectful, empathetic letter to the executor of the estate offering your services. Many wholesalers overlook this strategy because it requires a little extra legwork, which is exactly why it's less competitive.
5. Networking with Local Real Estate Professionals

Some of the best wholesale deals never get marketed publicly. They come through word of mouth. Build relationships with local real estate agents, property managers, estate attorneys, divorce attorneys, and contractors. Let them know you buy properties fast and in any condition. Attend your local REIA (Real Estate Investor Association) meetups monthly. Show up consistently and people will start thinking of you when a deal crosses their desk. Hot markets like [Atlanta](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/atlanta-ga), [Houston](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/houston-tx), and [Phoenix](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/phoenix-az) have especially active REIA communities worth plugging into.
6. Online Marketing and Social Media

Facebook Marketplace, Craigslist, and Google local search ads are underused by many wholesalers. Run ads targeting homeowners in your area with messaging like 'Sell your house fast, no repairs, no agents, no fees.' A basic Google Ads campaign targeting '[your city] sell my house fast' can generate motivated seller leads for $30 to $80 per lead. Build a simple landing page — even a free one through Carrd or Google Sites — and start capturing inquiries. Combine this with a strong social media presence in local neighborhood Facebook groups where sellers often post before going to an agent.

The investors who find the best deals aren't the luckiest — they're the most consistent. They show up in the same neighborhoods, mail to the same lists, and follow up with the same leads month after month until the timing is right for the seller.
How to Evaluate a Wholesale Deal Quickly

Finding a lead is only half the battle. You also need to move fast when a potential deal lands in your lap. The key metric in wholesaling is the Maximum Allowable Offer (MAO). The standard formula is: ARV x 70% minus repair costs minus your assignment fee. For example, if a property has an ARV of $200,000 and needs $30,000 in repairs, your MAO would be around $110,000 (assuming a $10,000 assignment fee). Use our free [Wholesale Deal Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator) to run these numbers instantly and know exactly what to offer before you ever pick up the phone.

Always leave room in your numbers. Aim for an assignment fee of at least $8,000 to $15,000 on residential deals. Going too thin on margin means one surprise repair cost can kill the deal for your buyer.
What to Do Once You Have a Deal Under Contract

Landing a motivated seller and getting a property under contract is a huge win — but you're not done yet. Now you need a buyer. This is where having a strong cash buyers list pays off. Read our guide on [how to find cash buyers for wholesale deals](https://aiwholesail.com/blog/how-to-find-cash-buyers-wholesale) to learn the fastest ways to locate investors ready to close. If you're starting from zero, our article on [how to build a cash buyers list from scratch](https://aiwholesail.com/blog/build-cash-buyers-list) walks you through every step.

You'll also need to decide how you want to exit the deal. Most beginners start with assignment contracts, which are simple and require no capital. But as you grow, you may want to explore double closings for deals where you don't want to disclose your assignment fee. Check out our breakdown of [double close vs assignment strategies](https://aiwholesail.com/blog/double-close-vs-assignment) to understand when each approach makes the most sense.
Building a Sustainable Deal Pipeline in Your Market

items: Pick 2 to 3 lead generation strategies and commit to them for at least 90 days before judging results
Follow up with every lead at least 5 to 7 times — most motivated sellers say yes after the third or fourth contact
Track every lead in a CRM so nothing falls through the cracks
Reinvest a portion of every deal's profit into your next marketing campaign
Focus on one target market area or zip code before expanding to new neighborhoods
Build systems so your pipeline keeps moving even when you're not actively working

sections.content: The investors who close the most deals aren't those who found one magic source of leads. They built repeatable systems. Whether you want to wholesale part-time from a single market or grow into a full operation, the fundamentals are the same. Start with what you can manage, execute consistently, and scale what works.
